options.rationale: Correct: an explicit deny always overrides any allow in IAM evaluation.

items.stem: Which TWO practices support least privilege in AWS IAM? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Grant only the specific actions and resources needed
options.rationale: Correct: scoping actions and resources is the core of least privilege.

options.text: Use roles with temporary credentials instead of long-lived keys
options.rationale: Correct: temporary credentials reduce the risk of leaked static keys.

options.text: Share one access key across the whole team
options.rationale: Shared keys remove accountability and over-permit.

items.explanation: Correct: both keyed options are right; the distractors are wrong for the reasons given.

items.stem: An application on an EC2 instance needs to read from an S3 bucket. What is the recommended way to grant this?

options.text: Attach an IAM role to the instance with a scoped S3 read policy
options.rationale: Correct: an instance role provides temporary, scoped credentials without static keys.

options.text: Embed a long-lived access key in the application code
options.rationale: Hardcoded keys are a major security risk.
Public buckets expose data far beyond the app's needs.
Admin far exceeds a bucket-read requirement.

items.explanation: Correct: an instance role provides temporary, scoped credentials without static keys.
